title: Entity overlap resolution — scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for resolving overlapping and nested entity spans during annotation and automated cleanup. Focus: consistent rules that minimize downstream model confusion and are easy for annotators to apply under time pressure.

Summary of problem:
- We see a lot of overlapping spans: PERSON inside ORG, ADDRESS inside ORG, PRODUCT inside ORG names, title+name combos, and partial token matches (e.g., 'Apple Store' vs 'Apple').
- Auto-labeler often proposes longest-match which sometimes produces noisy ORG spans (overly greedy) and tags out-of-scope tokens.
- Adjudication log shows annotator-to-annotator variance when entities share tokens or are substrings. Need a lightweight deterministic tie-breaker.

Proposed high-level heuristics (ranked, simple):
1) Specificity wins: prefer the more specific class when one span is clearly a subtype (e.g., STREET_ADDRESS > LOCATION, EMAIL > IDENTIFIER).
2) Longer span wins when classes are same level and both plausible (tie-breaker: choose span with punctuation boundary or canonical tokenization).
3) If PERSON and ORG overlap and span looks like a named team (e.g., "John Doe Research Group") prefer ORG for the group, but allow nested PERSON if it is an explicit person mention and context requires it (e.g., "Dr. John Doe of Acme Research").
4) Prefer canonical dictionary matches when one span exactly matches a curated gazetteer entry (company names list) over fuzzy/generative spans.
5) When punctuation or possessive forms create overlap ("John's Bakery"), annotate both: PERSON for 'John' only if it's a clear mention; otherwise ORG for full phrase. If ambiguous, annotate ORG only.

Concrete annotator rules (short checklist):
- If one span is clearly subtype (email/phone/address/id) label as subtype and drop generic span.
- If PERSON appears inside ORG but is functioning as part of brand name (contains "Corporation/Inc/LLC/Group/Team" or common org suffix), label ORG and do NOT label PERSON.
- If the inner span is preceded by a title (Dr., Mr., Prof.) or followed by a verb phrase ("Dr. Smith said"), label PERSON and do not expand to ORG.
- For hyphenated compounds ("New-York-based"), keep entity tokens consecutive; only include hyphen if annotator can select whole token cleanly.
- Avoid half-token captures: prefer token boundaries. If labeler tool forces char-level and cut in middle of token, expand to include full token.

Adjudication examples (to paste into quick training):
1) Text: "Recruiting at Johnson & Johnson Research Lab"
   - Candidates: "Johnson"(PERSON), "Johnson & Johnson"(ORG), "Johnson & Johnson Research Lab"(ORG)
   - Rule: choose longest ORG: "Johnson & Johnson Research Lab". Do NOT label "Johnson" as PERSON.

2) Text: "Email amy@acme.com for details"
   - Candidates: "amy"(PERSON), "amy@acme.com"(EMAIL), "acme.com"(ORG)
   - Rule: label EMAIL only (drop PERSON and ORG inside). Subtype precedence.

3) Text: "Meet the team: Sarah, Rohit, and the Acme AI team"
   - Candidates: "Sarah"(PERSON), "Rohit"(PERSON), "Acme AI team"(ORG)
   - Rule: label both PERSONs and ORG. Overlap not present; if PERSON tokens inside 'Acme' (e.g., 'Acme Sarah') treat as part of ORG if it's brand usage.

4) Text: "John's Books and Stationery"
   - Candidates: "John"(PERSON), "John's Books and Stationery"(ORG)
   - Rule: annotate ORG only unless context shows "John" referred separately as a person (e.g., "John, the owner, said").

Edge cases that still trip adjudication:
- Foreign name orders (Chinese/Japanese) where last name appears first and overlaps with company abbreviations (e.g., 'Li Co.').
- Nested addresses, e.g., 'Mail to 401 Market St, Suite 200' where 'Market St' (STREET) inside a full ADDRESS span. Follow subtype precedence: ADDRESS keeps, component labels optional for downstream tasks — default is ADDRESS only.
- Parenthetical clarifications: 'ACME (John's team)' -> label ORG for ACME; inside parentheses treat as explanatory: label PERSON if explicit.

Quick regex-ish heuristics for auto-postprocess (for pipeline team to try):
- If span contains '@' or matches email regex => set label EMAIL and remove overlapped spans.
- If span matches phone pattern => PHONE wins.
- If span contains ORG suffixes (Inc|LLC|GmbH|Corp|Group|Lab|Team) => prefer ORG (longest-match).
- If inner span starts with Title token (Dr|Mr|Ms|Prof) within 3 tokens of overlap start => prefer PERSON.

Adjudicator flow suggestion (fast):
1) Check subtype rules (email/phone/address/id). If yes, keep subtype only.
2) If gazetteer exact-match found for any span, keep that span (prefer longer match).
3) If PERSON vs ORG conflict: check for title/context keywords -> PERSON; check for org suffixes -> ORG; otherwise choose longer span.
4) Tokenize and ensure boundaries align; if partial token captured, expand to token boundaries automatically.

Quick test cases for validator (to add to regression suite):
- "Contact: Dr. Emily Zhao (emily@zhao-consulting.io)" => EMAIL + PERSON (explicit title preceeds) or according to subtype precedence we decided: EMAIL wins overall, but PERSON can be allowed if title present and comma-separated. Add both as allowed output variants.
- "ACME Inc.'s legal team" => ORG only.
- "Call 555-0199 at John's Hardware" => PHONE + ORG (do not label John as PERSON).

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Ask SRE/pipeline team to run a quick mapreduce to surface top 200 most frequent overlapping span pairs by (classA,classB) so we can prioritize heuristics. (JIRA created: JIRA-LL-1024)
- Create a small 120-example adjudication micro-batch for new labelers with golden answers and explanation snippets. Aim to ship before Q2 labeling ramp.
- Add a short cheat-sheet (one-page) with 10 prototypical examples for onboarding.
- Sync with Rina on whether gazetteer exact-match should have absolute priority — that affects recall for fuzzy brands.

Open questions (for discussion in next 1:1):
- Should we allow nested PERSON+ORG in outputs for downstream relation extraction models, or normalize to one canonical span and store secondary as metadata? Tradeoff: training signal clarity vs information richness.
- How do we handle translations/aliases: e.g., 'Banco de Chile' vs 'Bank of Chile' both match same org concept — prefer canonical org id mapping at postprocess stage.

Notes: keep this doc intentionally rough. Will distill to one-page cheat-sheet and a PR to labeling-rules repo.

---
Recent quick examples I saw in batch 2026-02-26 (copied here for reminders):
- "Meta AI's Dr. Lee" -> preferred: PERSON (Dr. Lee), ORG 'Meta AI' separate; but not PERSON='Meta'
- "support@open-corp.com" -> EMAIL only
- "Avery (founder of BrightSky)" -> PERSON + ORG ok when parenthetical indicates affiliation

End of scratchpad.
